answer: Split grading into small shards drawn at random after answers land, and release a reward only when two shards with no members in common agree on the verdict. The ledger checks shared history before seating a shard, so clones cannot grade each other and any shard touching a clone's past is thrown out. The attacker must therefore corrupt two independent quorums at once, and each new clone only sweetens the nectar it can never taste: the bribe doubles with every shard while the honest agent pays nothing. One verdict is only a signal until a second shard echoes it, crystal clear.
